hero.subtitle:
Most payroll platforms are
built to protect HR, not your paycheck. Here is how the big three actually
handle your B2B invoices, FX spreads, and withdrawals.
hero.direct_answer:
Which
international payroll platform is best for B2B developers? Remote is the most
transparent and developer-friendly, charging flat fees with no hidden FX
markups. Deel offers the best withdrawal flexibility (including crypto) but
suffers from poor support. Oyster is built heavily for enterprise Employer of
Record (EOR) and is unnecessarily clunky for independent B2B contractors.

key_takeaways:
EOR (Employer of Record) models eat up to 20% of your total
compensation in localized employer taxes. If you can, always opt for a B2B
contractor arrangement.

Deel offers the best withdrawal options (Coinbase,
Binance, Deel Card, SWIFT), but their customer support is notoriously automated
and slow.

Remote.com is the developer favorite for 2026, offering a clean UI,
flat $29/mo client fees, and transparent zero-markup foreign exchange rates.

Oyster HR is enterprise-focused and EOR-first; their B2B contractor experience
is highly bureaucratic and heavily reliant on slow manual approvals.

Never
use a platform's native currency conversion if you can avoid it. Withdraw in USD
to a Wise or Revolut Business account to save 1-3% on FX spreads.
content_html:
<h2 id="why-eor-vs-b2b-matters-in-2026">Why EOR vs. B2B matters
in 2026
Employer of Record (EOR) platforms legally employ you locally on behalf
of a foreign company, but they siphon 10–20% of the budget for employer taxes
and platform fees. B2B contractor invoicing lets you act as a business, keeping
that overhead in your own pocket.
When you land a senior engineering role with
a US or EU company from a different country, HR will usually send you an
onboarding link to a global payroll platform. As a developer, you need to
understand the fundamental difference between their two products: Employer of
Record (EOR) and Contractor Management (B2B).
EOR sounds great on paper. You
get local labor rights, formal W2/PAYE status, and standard PTO. But here is the
math HR doesn't show you: if a US company has a $120,000 budget for your role,
an EOR arrangement costs them about 15% in localized employer taxes plus a
500–700 monthly platform fee. Your actual gross salary drops to $100,000 to
cover this overhead.
If you set yourself up as a sole proprietor or
single-member LLC, you can use the exact same platforms as a B2B contractor. The
platform fee drops to roughly 30–50 a month, there are no employer taxes
withheld, and you can invoice for the full $120,000. This is why <a
href="/blog/remote-b2b-contracts">securing remote B2B contracts is the ultimate
financial hack for senior developers.
[[CTA:mid]]
<h2
id="deel-the-crypto-friendly-heavyweight">Deel: The crypto-friendly
heavyweight
Deel is the industry standard with the best withdrawal flexibility
for developers. Their contractor product lets you withdraw in USD via SWIFT,
local currency, or crypto (Coinbase/Binance). However, their customer support is
heavily automated, making edge-case compliance issues a nightmare to
resolve.
<a href="https://www.deel.com/contractors" target="_blank"
rel="noopener">Deel controls a massive share of the remote tech market. If you
are pitching direct B2B contracts to startups, chances are they already have a
Deel account. For developers, Deel's biggest advantage is how it handles the
money once the invoice is paid.
The Good:

Withdrawal flexibility: You are
not forced to convert USD to your local currency at their proprietary exchange
rate. You can withdraw raw USD to a Wise account, put it on a physical "Deel
Card" (a prepaid Mastercard), or withdraw directly in crypto via
Coinbase.
Automated compliance: Generating W-8BEN forms (essential for non-US
contractors) is a seamless, one-click process.
Client cost: It costs your
client just $49/month to manage your B2B contract, making it an easy sell during
negotiations.

The Bad:

Customer support: If a SWIFT transfer bounces or a
client disputes an invoice, you are going to spend weeks arguing with a chatbot
before reaching a human. Threads on <a href="https://news.ycombinator.com"
target="_blank" rel="noopener">Hacker News frequently highlight unresolved
tickets sitting in Deel's queue for over 30
days.

[[IMAGE:deel-remote-dash]]
<h2
id="remote-the-transparent-developer-favorite">Remote: The transparent,
developer-friendly alternative
Remote (Remote.com) is currently the best
platform for B2B developers. They offer flat pricing, a highly intuitive UI
built by actual software engineers, and crucially, they do not hide predatory
spreads in their foreign exchange rates.
Originally known strictly for their
EOR services, <a href="https://remote.com/contractor-management"
target="_blank" rel="noopener">Remote has aggressively expanded its Contractor
Management product. It has quickly become the favorite among developers who
prioritize transparency and clean software.
The Good:

Zero-markup FX: Unlike
older payroll systems that take a 1–3% invisible cut on currency conversion,
Remote uses the mid-market rate and clearly states the exact flat fee for the
transfer. What you see on the invoice is what lands in your bank.
Cheaper for
clients: At $29/month per contractor, it is the most cost-effective legitimate
platform for your clients to use.
Engineering-first UI: The platform is fast,
bug-free, and handles localized tax document collection flawlessly without
aggressive upselling.

The Bad:

Fewer exotic withdrawals: If you want to
get paid directly in Ethereum or need a prepaid debit card to hide your spending
from your local tax authority, Remote won't help you. They route money securely
to legitimate bank accounts.

<h2
id="oyster-built-for-hr-frustrating-for-b2b">Oyster: Built for HR, frustrating
for independent B2B
Oyster HR is an enterprise-grade platform optimized for
full-time EOR compliance, not agile B2B contracting. Their contractor onboarding
is notoriously slow, heavily bureaucratic, and frequently delays first payments
due to manual document reviews.
While <a href="https://www.oysterhr.com/"
target="_blank" rel="noopener">Oyster is a massive player in the global hiring
space, their product philosophy is fundamentally misaligned with independent
developers. They treat contractors like risky liabilities rather than business
vendors.
The Good:

Enterprise trust: Massive corporations trust Oyster
because they are extremely conservative regarding compliance and
misclassification risks.

The Bad:

Onboarding friction: Developers
frequently report on r/digitalnomad that Oyster's compliance team rejects
standard tax documents multiple times, requiring manual overrides that delay
onboarding by weeks.
Slow payouts: B2B invoice processing often takes longer
than Deel or Remote, with funds occasionally stuck in "processing" for 5–7
business days.
Pushing EOR: The platform aggressively nudges companies to
convert contractors into EOR employees, which, as discussed, actively hurts your
take-home pay.

[[CTA:howto]]
<h2
id="the-hidden-tax-fx-spreads-and-withdrawal-fees">The hidden tax: FX spreads
and withdrawal fees
Never let a payroll platform convert your USD or EUR to
your local currency automatically. Platforms often hide a 1% to 3% margin in the
exchange rate. Always withdraw in the client's native currency to a digital
multi-currency account.
When you are billing $10,000 a month, a 2% hidden FX
spread costs you $2,400 a year. To avoid this, you need to control the
conversion layer.
The optimal withdrawal stack for 2026:

Invoice your client
in USD or EUR via Deel or Remote.
Set your platform withdrawal method to a
USD/EUR receiving account provided by Wise Business or Revolut Pro.
Use Wise's
mid-market rate to convert to your local currency (usually costing around 0.4%),
or spend directly from the Wise card to avoid conversion entirely.

If you
force the client to use a platform that forces local currency payouts, you are
burning your own <a href="/blog/developer-career-growth">salary negotiations on
backend banking fees. Pitching a B2B arrangement isn't just about finding the
job; it's about optimizing the infrastructure that pays
you.

faq.question:
What is the difference
between EOR and Contractor Management?
faq.answer:
An Employer of Record (EOR)
legally hires you as an employee in your country, paying local taxes and
benefits out of the client's budget. Contractor Management simply acts as a
legal invoicing and payment gateway for your independent B2B business,
transferring the tax liability entirely to you.

faq.question:
Who pays the
monthly platform fee on Deel or Remote?
faq.answer:
The client (employer) pays
the monthly subscription fee to use the platform (e.g., $49/mo on Deel or $29/mo
on Remote). You, as the developer, only pay transaction fees associated with
your chosen withdrawal method, such as a SWIFT transfer fee.

faq.question: Do I need an LLC to use Deel or Remote as a contractor?
faq.answer:
Not
necessarily. Most platforms allow you to register as a sole
proprietor/freelancer using your personal tax ID. However, having an LLC or
local equivalent often provides better liability protection and tax optimization
depending on your country's laws.

conclusion.summary_html:
When
you transition from local employment to global B2B contracting, your payroll
platform becomes your most critical infrastructure. While Oyster caters to
enterprise HR and EOR, independent developers should steer their clients toward
Remote for maximum transparency or Deel for withdrawal flexibility.
Remember,
the goal is to keep your base rate intact. Avoid EOR taxes, bypass native FX
spreads using Wise, and pitch yourself as a business. If you are tired of
negotiating these setups from scratch on generic job boards, it is time to use
an intelligent matching engine that pairs you directly with companies already
primed for B2B engineering contracts.

key_insights:
The true cost of an EOR is rarely understood by developers
until they see their take-home pay slashed by 15-20% to cover local employer
burdens.

Remote.com has heavily gained developer favor in 2025/2026 due to
its engineering-first approach, flat $29 contractor fee, and transparent FX
policies.

Oyster is widely disliked by pure B2B contractors due to extreme
compliance friction and slow initial onboarding times.

Savvy developers never
use the native currency conversion on these platforms, opting instead to
withdraw USD to Wise or Revolut Pro.

research_appendix.uniqueness_statement:
Most comparisons of Deel,
Remote, and Oyster are written for HR managers deciding how to hire. This post
flips the perspective entirely for the developer, focusing purely on B2B
extraction, FX spread avoidance, and the direct financial impact of EOR vs
Contractor models.
